supporting_observations.claim: The periodic HTTPS activity matching the alert is attributable to the approved PixelForge updater: the updater process connected through the proxy to updates.pixelforge-suite.com at roughly five-minute intervals. One attempt received an authentication-required response; later attempts succeeded.
The PixelForge updater ran from its expected installation path under leo.martins’s interactive session, and created a temporary MSI file during the observed activity.

A network logon using sam.okafor’s account was recorded at WS-SOKAFOR-01 with WS-LMARTINS-01 as the originating workstation. This is inconsistent with the stated practice that remote administration is only done from WS-SOKAFOR-01, but the records do not establish who initiated or authorized it.
FILE-NWD-01 made an inbound RPC connection to WS-LMARTINS-01 during the review window. The records show the connection but do not identify the action performed over it.

DropboxUpdate.exe ran as SYSTEM on WS-LMARTINS-01, although Dropbox is not listed among approved services. The records show a DNS lookup for an akamaized.net name around the same time, but do not establish that DropboxUpdate.exe made an outbound connection or that file-sharing occurred.
The workstation made SMB, Kerberos, and LDAP connections to internal servers; the available records identify machine-account activity but do not show what data or commands, if any, were accessed.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records show CONNECT destinations, status, and byte counts, but not the HTTPS request or response contents; for example, the PixelForge tunnels are recorded in T046-00101 and T046-00157.
The DNS records for the akamaized.net name do not identify which process caused the lookup or prove a subsequent outbound connection; see T046-00124 and T046-00126.
The supplied records do not show the commands or resources involved in the FILE-NWD-01-to-workstation RPC connection; see T046-00067 through T046-00069.
claims_not_established: Whether sam.okafor’s network logon from WS-LMARTINS-01 was authorized or reflects credential misuse.
Whether the inbound RPC connection from FILE-NWD-01 was related to legitimate maintenance or unauthorized remote activity.
Whether Dropbox was installed or used for file sharing, or whether DropboxUpdate.exe communicated externally.
Whether any malicious payload, data theft, persistence, or other harmful action occurred.
additional_evidence_needed: Correlate with sam.okafor’s activity, endpoint logon/session records, and authorization or change records for the 13:26 UTC network logon.
Collect process and service installation history for Dropbox, plus network telemetry that attributes any outbound connection to a process.
Obtain RPC/service, SMB share-access, and file/process telemetry from FILE-NWD-01 and WS-LMARTINS-01 around 13:23–13:37 UTC.
Review endpoint and proxy telemetry for the full period to confirm whether the PixelForge updater was the process responsible for each periodic connection.
